methodology.collection: Google Ads Transparency Center inspected via live browser; primary websites read via web retrieval; publisher creative images inspected in browser.
methodology.scope: Five requested competitors. Three Google creatives per brand plus two historical Bland newsletter sponsorships.
methodology.sampling: Convenience sample from first visible domain results, not exhaustive or representative of budget allocation.
methodology.active_status: Google last-shown dates are captured independently. is_active, started_at and ended_at remain null because last shown is neither campaign activation nor termination.
methodology.copy: Headlines are short exact excerpts. body fields are explicitly paraphrased observations to avoid presenting invented ad text as exact transcription.
methodology.performance: No spend or performance inferred from ad count, creative longevity or wording. Historical publisher campaign claims remain source-scoped.
methodology.destinations: Google preview display URLs are recorded with link_url_kind=display_url; full redirect and final destination were not clicked.
methodology.ad_checks: Only completed searches are recorded. Other platform checking is handled separately by the main task.
methodology.creative_images: Google image URLs were matched to visible DOM image elements on the individually inspected creative page. Newsletter images come from the publisher's linked examples.

profile.category: AI voice infrastructure and agent platform
profile.positioning: Usage-based platform for deploying customer-service and receptionist agents without mandatory annual commitment.
profile.offer: Self-serve voice agents, chat agents and enterprise deployments.

pricing.conditions: Voice cost depends on LLM, voice, telephony and optional features; price calculator separates components.

sources.title: Retell AI official pricing
sources.summary: No required commitment for self-serve. Voice agents cost $0.07–$0.31/min, chat starts at $0.002/message, with $10 credits and 20 concurrent calls included. Enterprise uses custom pricing. Options affect total cost.

ads.headline: Humanlike AI Receptionist - AI Answers Every Call 24/7

The creative displays a 5.0 rating with 248 reviews and a sitelink claiming AI resolves 75% of calls; these are advertiser assertions, not measured ad performance.

ads.headline: Retell AI Voice Agent Platform - Enterprise Grade Voice AI
ads.body: Promotes handling calls and appointment booking while increasing capacity without hiring. Cites 600ms latency in the visible, truncated description.

ads.headline: Support Customers 24/7 - AI For Customer Service
ads.body: Promises continuous support coverage, routine issue handling and prompt escalation. Reduces integration concerns by describing SIP connection to an existing phone line and keeping the current helpdesk.
notes: First of two Google variations inspected.
Rendered body truncates after the helpdesk reference.

ad_checks.note: Visible domain summary reported 40 ads at any time/anywhere. Sample contains three individually inspected text creatives; counts are not active-ad totals.

insights.title: Retell separates receptionist and enterprise buying paths
insights.finding: Receptionist copy leads with continuous coverage and social proof; enterprise copy leads with capacity and latency; customer-service copy answers integration concerns.
insights.implication: A generic AI receptionist pitch enters an established category. Test a specific workflow or measurable deployment outcome against generic availability.

insights.title: No mandatory annual contract is a tangible pricing contrast
insights.finding: Retell's self-serve model differs from Synthflow's $30,000 annual enterprise starting point.
insights.implication: Segment prospects by willingness to implement and contract size instead of treating all voice platforms as equivalent SMB receptionist products.

profile.positioning: Enterprise voice automation with scoped implementation, telephony, integrations and security review.
profile.offer: Contracts start at $30,000 annually; detailed scope determines final price.

pricing.conditions: Final contract depends on volume, concurrency, telephony, integrations, security and launch support.

sources.title: Synthflow enterprise pricing
sources.summary: Annual enterprise engagements start at $30,000. Volume, concurrency, infrastructure, integrations and support shape final pricing; rollout includes implementation and enterprise security review.

notes: Paid competitor-comparison creative; do not attribute it to Retell merely because Retell appears in the headline.

insights.title: Synthflow buys competitor-evaluation intent
insights.finding: A Google ad names Retell and offers a review of its features, pricing and technical tradeoffs.
insights.implication: Comparison pages are a paid acquisition route. Create evidence-based comparisons with billing assumptions and deployment effort clearly stated.

insights.title: Scale and infrastructure frame the sale
insights.finding: One creative promotes million-call routing capacity and in-house infrastructure; another is localized in German. Official packaging now starts with an annual enterprise contract.
insights.implication: Focus comparisons on enterprise rollout requirements rather than repeating outdated low-priced no-code positioning.

profile.offer: AI calling with self-serve usage plans and enterprise implementation.

pricing.conditions: LLM and speech included; telephony billed separately. BYOT avoids transfer fees. Two trial credits and an inbound number are advertised.

notes: Publisher's campaign case study dated 2024-06-24 identifies paid newsletter placements and links this example. Actual individual send date was not disclosed.

ad_checks.note: Domain summary reported 71 ads, any time/anywhere. Three current Google text creatives individually inspected under verified Intelliga Corporation.
Paid publisher case study with two visible sponsorship examples. Historical campaign evidence; individual send dates unavailable.

insights.title: Bland pairs enterprise reassurance with a deadline
insights.finding: Outbound creative combines lead qualification, infrastructure control and compliance references with a 30-day launch promise.
insights.implication: Test a concrete implementation timeline backed by delivery capability; buyers are being sold a path to production, not just a natural-sounding demo.

insights.title: Speed to lead survives across formats
insights.finding: The historical newsletter promotes immediate qualification and scheduling; current Google outbound copy still emphasizes converting inbound interest into booked meetings.
insights.implication: Use lead response time and qualified meetings as hypotheses to test. The newsletter's 400% headline is not proof that a new campaign will achieve that result.

insights.title: Published clicks are historical and aggregate
insights.finding: TLDR reports over 20,000 clicks across its campaign, but gives no spend, CAC or attributable revenue.
insights.implication: Use the case study as evidence of paid newsletter distribution and response, not as a current performance benchmark or ROI forecast.

sources.summary: Human phone and chat service. Published plans include 200 minutes at $350, 300 at $395 and 400 at $575 monthly, with different setup and overage rates. Billing rounds to whole minutes, includes after-call work and exempts the first 30 sub-30-second interactions.

ad_checks.note: Three creatives inspected: two ANSWERCONNECT ads and one AnywhereWorks Canada, INC. banner visibly branded AnswerConnect. Total domain count not captured.

insights.title: Human presence is the creative proof
insights.finding: One image ad shows a named receptionist; another pairs a real-people headline with a message inbox. The website explicitly commits to human service.
insights.implication: AI brands compete against emotional reassurance as well as labor cost. Show escalation, call examples and successful outcomes if targeting buyers concerned about caller experience.

insights.title: Affordability depends on call mix
insights.finding: The search ad emphasizes simple pricing; published plans add minute rounding, after-call time and tier-specific overage charges.
insights.implication: Use identical handled-minute and call-duration assumptions before comparing this service with AI usage pricing.

ads.body: Connects US-based receptionist support with the owner's ability to concentrate on work. Flexibility and cancellation are the headline objection-handling devices.
notes: The preview description is truncated.

ads.headline: PATLive - Highly Trained Receptionists
ads.body: Emphasizes US staffing, adaptable scripts and inclusive pricing; lists message taking and dispatch capabilities. Sitelinks reinforce affordable plans and a trial.
notes: First of two Google variations inspected.
This creative was last shown more than a month before observation; Google did not expose a confirmed end date or active status.
Display destination was outside the inspected crop, so link_url is null.

ad_checks.note: Domain summary reported 12 ads at any time/anywhere, under verified PATLive, Inc. Three text creatives inspected; the sample includes one last shown August 2.

insights.title: The $49 hook needs usage context
insights.finding: PATLive's live Google creative leads with $49/month. That official entry plan includes no minutes; 100 minutes would cost $348 before tax if kept on that plan.
insights.implication: Compare included minutes and overage together. PATLive's published 100-minute package is $189, demonstrating why the entry price alone misrepresents likely cost.

insights.title: Flexible commitment and human staffing answer different objections
insights.finding: One creative sells cancellation flexibility while another stresses US-based trained receptionists. The trial reduces switching friction.
insights.implication: Test low-risk onboarding separately from service-quality reassurance rather than placing every benefit in one generic ad.
